summary: Ran repository-wide type checks (passed clean across 12 workspace projects) and the agent-server discover-resources test suite (failed: 20 of 100 tests). Then computed a sha256 of the diff for four targeted files and printed line ranges from three Svelte/TS files to confirm specific findings.
decisions: Resources, agents-files, and skills must use non-absolute relative paths and proper `..${sep}` boundary checks so Windows cross-drive paths (e.g. D: vs C:) are not silently misclassified as project resources with `project/*` IDs.

All canonical resource roots must be derived from Pi's `getAgentDir()` (or an injected agent directory) rather than hardcoded `homedir()/.pi/agent`, so that `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` is respected consistently across resource roots and extension management.

The Pi Web branch in `pi-agent-service` must apply the same catalog-selected skill paths/no-skills configuration as the normal branch (via `ResourceCatalogService.enabledSkillPaths()`) so Pi-discovered skills honor Gizmo enablement and per-project overrides.

Extension discovery should reuse Pi's package/resource resolution instead of a divergent scanner that misclassifies `index.js`, `package.json` `pi.extensions`, top-level symlinks, and `.mts/.mjs/.cts/.cjs` files.

Provider extensions must be registered before model runtime selection in the normal branch (e.g. via `createAgentSessionServices` or flushing pending registrations) so a provider-only setup can select an initial model.

Skill editing must be restricted to declared canonical managed skill roots with `realpath` containment, and an `editable` capability must be exposed to the client to prevent writes to bundled-extension or symlink-escaped skill paths.

Saving a skill must validate with Pi's skill parser before replacing the file; on failure the editor must remain open with diagnostics so a malformed frontmatter cannot drop the skill from the catalog and lock it out.

The global settings page must always load the intended global catalog on entry (or carry catalog scope through edit requests) to avoid presenting workspace-catalog skills as editable when the server only authorizes against a global-only catalog.

Skill writes must include optimistic-concurrency metadata (revision/mtime) and the editor must guard against unsaved changes on Cancel/Escape/backdrop to prevent silent overwrites and accidental data loss.
Both WebSocket reads and writes must validate skill content against the shared `skillFileSchema` (including the 1 MB cap), so an oversized skill cannot be loaded for editing but blocked on save.

Discover-resources tests must be migrated alongside the canonical-folder behavior and extended to cover cross-drive Windows paths, custom Pi agent directories, extension manifests, symlinks, and editor path containment.
errors: `pnpm --filter @gizmo/agent-server test -- tests/resources/discover-resources.test.ts` failed with 20 of 100 tests failing across 5 files. `packageResourceRoots`/`extensionResourceRoots` returned `{ skills: [], prompts: [] }` instead of expected temp-directory paths because it does not resolve extension package roots. `discoverResources` returned Pi-loaded skills (`archify`, `svelte-code-writer`, `svelte-core-bestpractices`, `impeccable`) instead of only the expected `review`, and emitted a project-scoped entry whose discovery record lacked a `source` field. `runScript` tests threw `Script must be inside the workspace: <name>` from the workspace containment guard at `src/scripts/run-script.ts:60` instead of the expected shell/not-found/timeout/bun errors. `PiSessionRepository` catalog restored sessions keyed by Windows-style `C:\...` workspace paths rather than the `/projects/game`/`/projects/tools` paths the test asserted. `pi-runtime-config` tests for missing Pi config and explicit Pi auth re-import failed (2 of 5).
